title: NLP tracks emergency abdominal CT findings during the COVID-19 pandemic
summary: Random forest NLP classifiers trained on 2448 annotated reports identified appendicitis, diverticulitis and bowel obstruction in 22,182 emergency department CT reports, with cross-validated accuracies of 0.97-0.99 and F1 0.86-0.91. Applied to all reports, estimated case numbers fell 43-57% in April 2020 compared with 2018-2019, then rebounded, while proportions of CT studies with these pathologies did not significantly increase.
ai_technology: Random forest natural language processing classifiers on radiology report impressions

evidence.tested: Five-fold cross-validation of classifiers and application to all reports from one urban emergency department.
evidence.unknown: Single health system; no external validation of the classifiers; causes of the decline are inferred; full text not reviewed.
evidence.ai_role: NLP classifiers counted pathology from reports at scale.

source_review.scope: Abstract read from Europe PMC metadata for this DOI. Author affiliations and publisher full text not accessed. Author affiliations from OpenAlex metadata.
